goals: Unify external OSINT collectors behind a typed adapter contract.
Persist a provenance-first entity graph and resumable workflow checkpoints.
Add nine isolated domain/infrastructure adapters without rewriting upstream tools.
Enforce legal-only routing and explicit authorization for target-adjacent DNS/recon actions.
Preserve per-fact provenance: value, tool, source URL, timestamp, confidence.
Add legal-gated identity, email, and phone adapters without reimplementing upstream tools.
Prevent credential values from entering Docker argv or Aletheia audit command records.
Add selected social, geospatial, and image-analysis adapters using official APIs or existing upstream packages.
Keep biometric/image analysis offline or explicitly credentialed; do not perform person identification against remote databases.
Add corporate, regulatory-records, and sanctions adapters using verified official/public or licensed APIs.
Keep sanctions search relevance distinct from identity/match probability and require source verification before legal assertions.

tool_inventory.name: ssl_tls
tool_inventory.license: Composite adapter; sub-sources are the Qualys SSL Labs assessment API v4, the Debian bookworm testssl.sh and sslscan packages, and the CertGraph and tlsx Go modules
tool_inventory.invocation: Local command line tools (testssl, certgraph, sslscan, tlsx) dispatched by sub-source plus the Qualys SSL Labs assessment API v4, via dedicated Docker runner (aletheia/ssl-tls:v1)
tool_inventory.legal_notes: Composite adapter covering the five verified sub-sources of the ssl_tls batch: qualys-ssl-labs (Qualys SSL Labs assessment API v4), testssl (testssl.sh, Debian bookworm package 3.0.8+dfsg-1), certgraph (CertGraph v0.1.3, go install github.com/lanrat/certgraph@v0.1.3), sslscan (Debian bookworm package 2.0.7-1) and tlsx (v1.4.0, go install github.com/projectdiscovery/tlsx/cmd/tlsx@v1.4.0). Four sub-sources are local command line tools installed in the image and invoked by the runner as subprocesses with an argv list; no shell string is ever built, so an input value cannot be interpreted as shell syntax. Every documented invocation, endpoint, authentication requirement, documented rate limit, documentation URL and version pin is recorded in docker/ssl_tls/RATE_LIMITS.md, each with the source of its pin, and no flag, endpoint or version was inferred from an example response. The Qualys SSL Labs v4 analyze call documents a mandatory email request header holding the address registered through the free registration API and answers 441 for an unregistered client; the runner sends the header only when SSLLABS_EMAIL is set, never prints it and never records it, and otherwise reports the sub-source as a documented skip. sslscan, certgraph and tlsx publish no severity classification, so their records are recorded with severity 'info' rather than an invented rating; only the severities and letter grades the sources themselves publish (testssl.sh OK/INFO/WARN/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL and SSL Labs endpoint grades) are normalized. Direct probes connect to the target service, so a run needs authorisation and the adapter requires the assertion; no sub-source needs a paid key and no credential is stored in this repository.

tool_inventory.name: email_auth
tool_inventory.license: Composite adapter; sub-sources are the keyless scan.mx email-authentication HTTPS API and the Apache-2.0 checkdmarc library
tool_inventory.invocation: Keyless scan.mx HTTPS JSON API plus the locally installed checkdmarc library, via dedicated Docker runner (aletheia/email-auth:v1)
tool_inventory.legal_notes: Composite adapter covering the two verified sub-sources of the email_auth batch: scan-mx (the keyless scan.mx email-authentication JSON API, GET https://api.scan.mx/v1/check?domain=<domain>) and checkdmarc (the Apache-2.0 checkdmarc Python library, called through its documented entry point checkdmarc.check_domains, pinned at 6.0.4 from PyPI). Both candidates were verified from their own official documentation, so nothing is dropped. Every endpoint, query-parameter name, authentication requirement, documented rate limit, documentation URL and version pin was read from the provider's own documentation and is recorded in docker/email_auth/RATE_LIMITS.md; none was inferred from an example response. Neither sub-source needs a credential, the descriptor declares no secret environment variable, and no key is stored in this repository. The runner classifies the seed as a fully qualified domain name before either sub-source is called, because scan.mx answers HTTP 422 for anything else; a non-FQDN is reported as a documented skip. An email-authentication record is a DNS observation of a domain's published mail configuration, not a statement about the organisation operating it or its reputation. Every run contacts a third-party API and third-party DNS resolvers, so it needs authorisation and the adapter requires the assertion.
tool_inventory.note: Two sub-sources implemented after verifying each provider's own documentation: scan-mx (https://api.scan.mx/, keyless with no signup, GET /v1/check?domain=, JSON; documented limit not published) and checkdmarc (https://domainaware.github.io/checkdmarc/api.html, documented importable entry point checkdmarc.check_domains, Apache-2.0). phase_1_scope.graph_store: File-backed JSON graph and checkpoint stores are current; production database backends remain future work
phase_1_scope.durable_orchestrator: checkpointed local DAG runner in Phase 1; Temporal/Celery integration boundary reserved

known_environment_limitations: The historical local environment had no Docker CLI or Docker socket. Hosted CI verified 34 Docker cases before the approved removals; the current 31-case set has not yet been run in CI.
InsightFace requires operator-provisioned model weights because the container intentionally has no network path for model download.
Production-grade outbound-request auditing for opaque CLI/API collectors still requires enforced egress/proxy telemetry beyond adapter invocation logs.
The Phase 7 web UI is intentionally unauthenticated for local development and must be placed behind authentication before non-local exposure.

phase_2_scope.entity_resolution: type-aware canonical normalization + exact deduplication + conservative fuzzy SAME_AS_CANDIDATE edges
phase_2_scope.automatic_merge_policy: exact canonical match only; fuzzy similarity never authorizes merge
phase_2_scope.integrity: canonical report content SHA-256 + per-artifact SHA-256
phase_2_scope.production_note: PDF is a provenance-preserving technical report, not a jurisdiction-independent guarantee of admissibility.

phase_3_scope.docker_isolation: Each new upstream tool has its own dedicated Docker image; GPL tools are kept as separate processes/images.
phase_3_scope.credential_handling: Shodan secrets are explicit allowlisted environment variables and are not embedded in commands or results; Phase 4 follows the same invariant.
phase_3_scope.source_provenance_policy: Where upstream CLI output lacks per-record URLs, the finding distinguishes collector provenance from primary-source provenance and hashes raw evidence.

phase_4_scope.identity_policy: Claimed/positive account signals are retained; negative/error/rate-limited states are excluded from the graph as identity facts.
phase_4_scope.email_policy: No password fields are emitted. HIBP is authenticated breach-account lookup only. h8mail is restricted to a bounded non-premium mode.
phase_4_scope.phone_policy: libphonenumber is offline parsing/validation; PhoneInfoga requires explicit authorization assertions.
phase_4_scope.credential_handling: Secrets are injected by Docker inherited environment names only; secret values are excluded from command argv, audit records, and result JSON.
phase_4_scope.docker_isolation: Every selected upstream tool has its own Docker image; GPL tools are separate processes/images.

deferred_reason.whatsmyname: Current upstream project is a community dataset and its bundled checker scripts were removed; implementing a new checker would violate the adapter-not-rewrite boundary.
deferred_reason.blackbird: Current upstream packaging/version/license was not sufficiently verified to make a truthful pinned adapter in this phase.
deferred_reason.namechk: Current official API packaging/licensing/entitlement details were not sufficiently verified for a pinned adapter in this phase.

validation.unit_and_contract_tests: 67 passed, 34 skipped (historical pre-removal local baseline; not rerun after removals).
validation.integration_tests: 31 configured Docker cases after the approved removals; not rerun in this worktree.
validation.integration_skip_breakdown: 3 Phase 1 + 9 Phase 3 + 6 Phase 4 + 7 Phase 5 + 5 Phase 6 + 1 Phase 7 = 31 configured cases.
validation.security_tests: passed: authorization gates; secret values excluded from Docker argv/audit records; benchmark quality metrics require labels.

phase_5_scope.biometric_policy: Detection only. No remote face search, no person-identification claims, and no demographic inference.
phase_5_scope.credential_policy: Reddit and YouTube secrets are allowlisted environment variables and excluded from argv/audit command records.
phase_5_scope.model_policy: Offline face adapters never fetch model weights at runtime; model files must be operator-provisioned when required.
phase_5_scope.deferred_reason: Current access/version/license or model-provisioning details were not sufficiently pinned to integrate without guessing or creating replacement implementations.

phase_6_scope.authorization_policy: All Phase 6 network adapters require explicit authorization_assertion and legal_only=true.
phase_6_scope.credential_policy: OpenCorporates and OpenSanctions secrets are allowlisted Docker environment variables; CourtListener token is optional and likewise never placed in argv.
phase_6_scope.evidence_policy: Search results are discovery observations. Sanctions search score is not identity/match probability; court results require review of the underlying legal source.
phase_6_scope.deferred_reason: Exact current endpoint/access/licensing or jurisdiction-specific contracts were not sufficiently verified to implement without guessing. PACER remains paid/credentialed and is not accessed by this phase.

phase_7_scope.benchmarking: SQLite benchmark_cases + execution_samples; labeled quality metrics and unlabeled execution telemetry are kept distinct.
phase_7_scope.leaderboard: Sorted by labeled recall/precision then observed execution speed; missing quality labels remain null.
phase_7_scope.web_ui: FastAPI root page with local interactive SVG graph, node details, run metadata, and benchmark leaderboard.
phase_7_scope.mcp_transport: stdio JSON-RPC bridge using the same orchestrator and legal gates.
phase_7_scope.production_note: Authentication, rate-limited remote MCP, PostgreSQL/Neo4j/Elasticsearch/MinIO/Redis production backends remain deployment work; Phase 7 keeps deterministic local stores.
